extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals / PR pros pitching journalists
extracted.subtask_description: Practical guidance for crafting short, personalized email pitches to journalists to secure coverage, interviews, or commentary. Focuses on subject lines, salutations, openings, body, closing, word counts, and effective pitch patterns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: 6-10 words ideal
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the subject line to roughly six to ten words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise length helps readability and opens; reiterated in Word Count Limits (subject line: 6-10 words).

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: Front-load the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Put the newsworthy element at the start of the subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the most important, attention-getting information appear first so recipients see the news immediately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: Avoid promotional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not use language that reads like marketing copy or hype in the subject line.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep it factual and news-focused rather than salesy or clickbait-y.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: Test against "would I open this?"
rubrics_metrics.description: Use your own judgment — would you open the email based on that subject line?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A simple litmus test to evaluate whether the subject line is compelling and appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject line: No misleading "exclusive" claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not claim an 'exclusive' unless it is truly exclusive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid dishonest or misleading framing that will erode trust with the journalist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salutation: First name only
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the reporter by their first name (e.g., 'Hi Sarah').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Casual, direct salutations are preferred over overly formal openings in outreach emails.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salutation: Avoid generic salutations
rubrics_metrics.description: Never use 'Dear Reporter' or placeholder tokens like '[FIRST NAME]'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic salutations signal mass blasts and reduce credibility; always personalize.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salutation: Make sure name is spelled correctly
rubrics_metrics.description: Verify spelling of the recipient's name before sending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A misspelled name undermines personalization and can immediately sour the contact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Salutation: Verify the byline is current
rubrics_metrics.description: Check that the recipient still writes the beat or holds the byline you reference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Confirming current role prevents pitching the wrong person and wasting both parties' time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening sentence: Reference specific recent work
rubrics_metrics.description: Start by noting a particular recent article or piece the journalist wrote.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite a specific story to demonstrate relevance and show you've done your homework.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening sentence: Demonstrate you've read them
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the opening to show familiarity with the reporter's work rather than broad flattery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete references are preferred over generic praise; signals targeted outreach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening sentence: Avoid generic pleasantries
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not open with lines like 'Hope you're doing well.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Skip formulaic greetings that add no value and waste space in a short pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening sentence: Avoid 'I came across your article'
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid wording that sounds like you only casually encountered the reporter's work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Phrases that imply surface-level attention weaken the impression of genuine familiarity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opening sentence: Be specific (example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use concrete phrasing such as 'Loved your piece on X published Tuesday' to show specificity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the article/topic and timing to anchor your reference and prove recency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: One news item per pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Pitch only a single news item in each email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeping to one story reduces cognitive load and increases the chance of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: Story angle clear within 2 sentences
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the central news angle obvious within the first two sentences of the body.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Journalists scan quickly; surface the hook up front so they immediately understand the value.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: Concrete numbers where possible
rubrics_metrics.description: Include specific statistics or quantifiable details when available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numbers make claims more credible and provide clear hooks for reporters ('We surveyed 1,000 X...').

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: Source credentials in 1 sentence
rubrics_metrics.description: Summarize the spokesperson or source's qualifications in a single sentence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A concise credential line (e.g., '30 years of expertise in X') supports the source's credibility without verbosity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Body: Visual assets linked, not attached
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide links to images, video, or other assets rather than attaching files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Linked assets avoid large attachments that may be blocked and allow journalists to preview and download as needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing: Single clear ask
rubrics_metrics.description: End with one unambiguous ask (e.g., interview? data? exclusive?).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A single ask reduces ambiguity and makes it easy for the journalist to respond.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing: Time-bound offer
rubrics_metrics.description: Make the offer time-bound (e.g., today, this week, by Friday).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stating a timeframe creates urgency and helps reporters plan coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing: Phone number + calendar link
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a direct phone number and a calendar link for scheduling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide immediate ways to connect to lower friction for quick interviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Closing: Backup contact if unavailable
rubrics_metrics.description: Give an alternate contact if you will be unavailable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the journalist can still get what they need even when the primary contact is out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count: Subject line: 6-10 words
rubrics_metrics.description: Subject lines should be kept within six to ten words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reinforces the Subject Line Rules and supports overall brevity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count: Body: 100-200 words total
rubrics_metrics.description: Keep the email body between 100 and 200 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concise bodies respect journalists' time and facilitate quick evaluation of the pitch.

rubrics_metrics.name: Word count: Total email: under 250 words
rubrics_metrics.description: The complete email (subject + body + closing) should be under 250 words.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain tightness across all sections to maximize readability and response likelihood.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Pattern: The Data Pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: 'We surveyed 1,000 X about Y. The surprising finding: [specific stat]. Full report attached. Available for interview.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when you have original data or survey results; lead with the key statistic and offer the full report and interview availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Pattern: The Trend Pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: 'Following your piece on [trend], we have data showing [related insight]. CEO available for follow-up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tie your pitch to existing coverage of a trend to demonstrate relevance and offer an on-the-record spokesperson.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Pattern: The Source Pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: 'For your ongoing coverage of [beat], [Name] at [Company] is uniquely positioned to comment on [topic]. 30 years of expertise in [area].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when proposing a subject-matter expert as commentary or background source rather than newnews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pitch Pattern: The Exclusive Pitch
rubrics_metrics.description: Structure: 'Offering you first look at [news] before broader release. Embargo until [date/time]. Phone interview available now.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offer exclusives judiciously with clear embargo terms and immediate access to spokespeople to maximize pickup.
